source_snapshot.procedure: Enable BIOS OS Watchdog Timer, disable Windows automatic restart, run the attached High IRQ fault utility and expect a blue screen/watchdog reboot within ten minutes plus fatal-reset POST warning; then disable the BIOS watchdog, repeat the fault and expect a hang without reboot.
source_snapshot.criteria: Verify exact Watchdog Timer help and Enabled/Disabled choices, default reset to Disabled, WDAT offset 03Ch bit 0 set while Enabled, and WDAT absent while Disabled.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL is an unrelated 100-AC-cycle procedure copied from duplicate row 1525 and exposes BMC credentials; it has no runtime watchdog, BIOS or WDAT coverage.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED correctly separates enabled/disabled states and rejects the AC-cycle substitution, but treats runtime versus WDAT as a choice. Direct source and adjacent-row review support preserving both as independent mandatory checkpoints.

old_problem: The historical review retained Pending, Source Conflict and BLOCKED because `loader Watchdog`, the OS-watchdog High IRQ procedure and BIOS UI/WDAT criteria describe different evidence layers, while the attached fault utility, timeout oracle and recovery were missing. The same code also identifies row 1525's unrelated AC Cycle 100 times case.
disposition_reason: No layer is selected away. Treat `loader Watchdog` as this row's preserved label, not authorization to invent a bootloader stimulus, and require four linked gates: BIOS UI/default; Enabled-state WDAT; Enabled-state controlled High IRQ expiry/reset/POST warning; and Disabled-state WDAT absence plus non-reset hang for the approved observation window. Row 804 proves the criteria belong to a separately expressible BIOS/WDAT flow, while row 803 explicitly adds runtime enabled/disabled behavior; both must pass independently. The missing signed High IRQ tool, exact platform timeout/table profile and manual hang recovery are bounded Project packages. Their absence makes execution NOT READY, but does not require a new engineering choice or justify substituting 100 AC cycles.
decision_basis: XLSX row 803, physical adjacent row 804, duplicate-code row 1525, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. Formal queue sequence 20 is row 805 / variant 8443c6f5a25fe6ca.

Duplicate row 1525 / variant b994bd521c15eba8 is Sanity FW Matrix `AC Cycle 100 times`, has a different script and 720-minute machine time, and expressly expects no blue screen. It is incompatible with this row's deliberate High IRQ crash/watchdog reset and cannot contribute evidence.

UEFI's ACPI-related specification registry recognizes WDAT as the Watchdog Action Table. The source's offset 03Ch bit 0 requirement is handled as a versioned WDAT Flags/Enabled contract and must be decoded from a complete checksum-valid table by an approved parser; a fixed F000h physical address or guessed layout is not used.

WDAT/UI data shows advertised firmware capability/configuration; it cannot prove that the OS initialized and serviced the watchdog, that expiry reset the host, or that reset-cause/POST reporting worked. Runtime evidence likewise cannot prove the exact help, default or WDAT bytes.

Enabled and Disabled are phases, not a contradiction: the source procedure explicitly changes the single BIOS setting and uses the same approved fault stimulus to require reset in one state and no watchdog reset in the other. Each state has a distinct WDAT and runtime oracle.

An unvalidated privileged High IRQ utility can corrupt active I/O, hang before logs flush or trigger a reboot loop. It must have exact hash/source, supported OS/driver/BIOS, invocation and demonstrated fault semantics; no generic bugcheck, stress, AC cycle or guessed substitute is accepted.

ED-02 preserves duplicate identities; ED-03/ED-13 reject unrelated or guessed commands; ED-06 keeps power/reset mechanisms distinct; ED-11 limits BIOS changes to one approved reversible setting; ED-16 prevents a short observation from replacing the required interval; ED-17/ED-25 keep destructive actions attended; ED-19 protects evidence; ED-20/ED-23 require real UI/POST visual evidence; ED-28 requires authorized fault semantics, isolation and recovery; ED-29 requires full state recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 preserve package, confirmation and verdict ownership.

test_case.test_name: loader Watchdog: BIOS UI, WDAT and OS runtime enabled/disabled matrix
test_case.purpose: Verify the exact BIOS watchdog UI/default and state-dependent WDAT contract, then prove with the same approved High IRQ stimulus that Enabled causes a bounded watchdog reset and fatal-reset POST indication while Disabled does not cause a watchdog reset during the full observation interval, followed by controlled manual recovery and restoration.
required_package: Exact platform BIOS/BMC/ACPI/OS build and Project OS Watchdog profile: setting path, help text, choices, default, WDAT signature/revision/layout/checksum, Enabled flag at byte 0x3C bit 0, Disabled-state table-absence requirement, timer owner, configured timeout and tolerance

Approved complete ACPI table acquisition and WDAT decoder that operates on a checksum-valid table; if Project acceptance still requires ICE/F000h inspection, an authorized firmware engineer, exact BIOS.MAP/table address and visual/raw-memory evidence are additionally required

Signed/hashed High IRQ utility and driver with authoritative owner, source/version, exact invocation, privilege, supported OS/BIOS, demonstrated fault effect, cleanup/uninstall and explicit statement that it tests the intended watchdog path

Dedicated non-production SUT with writes/services quiesced, current backup and recovery media, crash-dump/pagefile capacity, OS event and BMC SEL export, serial/OOB console, independent monotonic timer and boot-loop escape

Enabled/Disabled state matrix specifying Windows automatic-restart state, expected crash display, configured watchdog expiry and maximum ten-minute source bound, reset cause, exact acceptable POST warning, disabled non-reset observation duration and manual hang recovery
Per-phase point-of-action approval, protected credential handling, BIOS backup/restore and final approved baseline; no plaintext command-line passwords
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED ATTENDED DESTRUCTIVE PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve/hash BIOS configuration, all ACPI tables, OS crash/watchdog settings, event logs, dumps and SEL; do not clear. Gate A: in BIOS visual setup, record the exact field/help/Enabled-Disabled choices, set Enabled only, save/reboot, and independently dump/validate WDAT; require the approved checksum/revision/layout and source byte-0x3C bit-0 result. Gate B: disable Windows automatic restart as specified, display the exact utility hash/invocation, timer, quiesce/backup, console, aborts and recovery, obtain immediate approval, start one independent timer and run the approved High IRQ stimulus once. Capture crash/hang, no OS self-restart, watchdog reset within the configured tolerance and no later than the source ten-minute limit, reset cause, exact POST warning, clean OS-ready recovery, dump/events/SEL. Gate C: enter BIOS, set Disabled, save/reboot, and prove the source-required absence of WDAT using the same complete-table method; if a valid WDAT remains, record FAIL/conflict-to-platform rather than silently changing the criterion. Gate D: after new confirmation run the identical fault once; require no watchdog reset throughout the full approved window at least covering the enabled timeout/ten-minute bound, then use only the pre-approved attended hang-recovery action. Restore BIOS watchdog and OS automatic-restart baseline, boot to OS Ready and verify data/filesystem, ACPI, logs, BMC and host health. Never run AC cycles, guess a fault command/table offset, clear first evidence, retry, or issue an automatic DUT verdict.
test_case.expected_result: The BIOS UI exposes the exact help and Enabled/Disabled choices and its default-reset action returns the field to Disabled. With Enabled, a complete valid WDAT matches the Project schema and byte 0x3C bit 0 equals one; one validated High IRQ event produces the intended visible crash/hang, watchdog-origin reset within the configured tolerance and ten-minute maximum, the exact fatal-reset POST warning and a clean recovery with correlated dump/event/SEL evidence. With Disabled, WDAT is absent as the source requires and the identical event does not watchdog-reset during the full observation window; attended recovery succeeds. Final BIOS/OS settings and system/data health match the approved baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires all four gates: exact UI/default, complete validated Enabled WDAT including 0x3C bit0, one approved enabled runtime expiry/reset/POST/OS-ready trace, source-required Disabled WDAT absence, and one same-stimulus disabled non-reset trace plus manual recovery and final restoration. AC cycles, a generic bugcheck, an unverified utility, WDAT alone, runtime reset alone, fixed-address bytes without table identity/checksum, reset outside tolerance, OS automatic restart mistaken for watchdog reset, missing reset cause/POST visual, premature disabled observation, unexpected reset/boot loop/data error, absent dump/log evidence, automatic retry or incomplete rollback cannot pass. Missing packages are NOT READY; a platform that retains WDAT when Disabled fails this exact criterion unless an authorized source change is recorded.
safety_gate: Use only a dedicated recoverable SUT. Quiesce writes/services, verify backup and recovery media, configure crash dumps, prove serial/OOB access and boot-loop escape before changing BIOS or launching the tool.
Change only the named watchdog setting, one state at a time. Capture the original BIOS/OS values and restore them at the end; no all/random BIOS modification is authorized.

A qualified engineer validates and launches the exact High IRQ package after immediate confirmation. Do not execute an unknown attachment, substitute another fault, expose credentials or run unattended.

Use independent timing and console capture. Stop and recover on wrong target/tool/hash, premature or repeated reset, unavailable dump/POST evidence, filesystem/data error, firmware/power/thermal fault, BMC/OOB loss or boot loop.
The Disabled phase intentionally hangs and has a pre-approved human recovery. Do not automatically reboot/power-cycle or repeat; preserve the first observation before recovery.
Never clear SEL, OS events or dumps before export/hash. After each phase verify clean OS Ready and evidence completeness before advancing.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, duplicate row-1525 exclusion, platform/BIOS/BMC/ACPI/OS/tool/driver identities and approved four-gate matrix
BIOS screenshots/video for field path, exact help, choices, default behavior and per-state value, plus backup/restore records
Complete raw ACPI table sets, RSDT/XSDT membership, WDAT signature/length/revision/checksum, decoded 0x3C bit0 and Disabled-state absence proof
Utility hash/source/signature/approval and time-aligned serial/OOB video, independent timer, crash screen/hang, watchdog reset cause, POST warning and OS-ready markers
Crash dumps, Windows events, BMC SEL/health and data/filesystem checks for Enabled and Disabled phases, with OS automatic-restart state proving it was not the reset source
Attended disabled-hang recovery, no automatic retry, final BIOS/OS/ACPI/host/BMC baseline and per-gate/overall engineer verdicts
test_case.recovery: For an unexpected reset, boot loop, dump failure, data error or lost console, do not rerun. Preserve OOB/SEL/available storage evidence, use the approved boot-loop escape or recovery media, restore the original watchdog and OS restart configuration, validate filesystem/data and escalate to the watchdog owner. For the expected Disabled hang, wait the complete authorized interval, capture the no-reset evidence, then perform only the pre-approved attended recovery; no automatic power action. If BIOS becomes inaccessible or WDAT/state cannot be reconciled, stop with the system isolated and use the platform BIOS recovery/rollback owner. Close only after clean OS Ready, restored settings, healthy BMC/platform and retained evidence hashes.
test_case.command: No executable fault command is emitted until the Project supplies and approves the exact High IRQ utility/driver contract. Read-only WDAT collection must use the approved complete-table acquisition path for the selected OS; firmware writes, AC cycles and direct physical memory assumptions are not authorized by this review.

source_conflict.reason: The procedure's dynamic Enabled/Disabled watchdog behavior and the Criteria's BIOS UI/WDAT obligations are made separate cumulative gates rather than alternatives. `loader Watchdog` remains the source label without invented bootloader coverage, and duplicate AC cycling remains excluded.

blocked.reason: Official ACPI/WDAT structure plus the explicit source phases permit a complete safe parameterized contract. The exact fault package, platform table profile, timeout and recovery are finite Project inputs; execution is NOT READY until supplied but no unresolved choice remains.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: BIOS UI/default and WDAT schema/disabled policy; exact High IRQ tool/driver/hash/semantics; timeout/reset/POST oracle; supported OS and crash settings; dedicated target, backup/dump/OOB/hang recovery, evidence and approval roles.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER DESTRUCTIVE CASE ONLY; NO BIOS, OS, WDAT, HIGH-IRQ, WATCHDOG, CRASH, REBOOT, AC, LOG, SEL, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.application: Identifies Watchdog Action Table (WDAT) as an ACPI-related specification. The review requires complete authoritative table discovery/validation rather than a guessed physical address.

external_authorities.title: ACPI Specification 6.6
external_authorities.application: Provides ACPI system-description-table discovery, headers and checksum framework used to prove table identity and integrity; WDAT-specific semantics remain bound to the approved WDAT/platform profile.

project_authority: The Project firmware, OS and watchdog owners approve the BIOS/WDAT matrix, exact High IRQ utility semantics, timeout/tolerance, reset-cause/POST oracle, disabled observation, destructive action, hang recovery and final baseline. They issue each gate and overall verdict; confirmation cannot make an AC cycle, unknown tool, incomplete table, OS auto-restart, missing dump, shortened wait or unexecuted phase PASS.
